rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so weights shift toward stronger obfuscation while respecting that flops-3 is a tiny (575-byte main) floating-point kernel where loop-body overhead directly multiplies into runtime. SUB is favored most: arithmetic substitution is nearly free at runtime and size and lands exactly on this program's dense FP/logic instruction mix, so its cost penalties stay low. FLA and BCF get strong security weights but elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost penalties so the selector applies them sparingly to the hot numeric loop rather than everywhere, since dispatcher and opaque-predicate overhead is most damaging in tight FP loops. SPLIT and IBR provide cheap structural diversity and are enabled moderately, with IBR's runtime penalty mid-range because indirect branching slows predictable branch-heavy kernels. ICALL and IGV are kept low-benefit here — the program has almost no indirect-call or global-variable surface — but remain in the table at reduced weights so they can fire on the few applicable sites without meaningful risk.
